question: Using Section 4I.06 and Figure 4I-4, describe the pedestrian interval order, minimum buffer interval, and walking speed normally used for clearance timing.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Per Section 4I.06 and Figure 4I-4, the pedestrian intervals occur in this order: the Walk interval (steady WALKING PERSON, 7 seconds minimum), followed immediately by the pedestrian change interval (flashing UPRAISED HAND, typically with countdown), followed by the buffer interval (steady UPRAISED HAND) before conflicting traffic is released. The buffer interval must always be provided and displayed, and Figure 4I-4 shows its minimum duration as 2 seconds. Pedestrian clearance time is normally computed using a walking speed of 3.5 feet per second, with slower speeds considered where slower pedestrians or wheelchair users routinely cross. Standards (mandatory): - From the Figure 4I-4 footnote: "The Buffer Interval, which shall always be provided and displayed, may be used to help satisfy the calculated pedestrian clearance time, or may begin after the calculated pedestrian clearance time has ended." Guidance (recommended): - "the pedestrian clearance time should be sufficient to allow a pedestrian crossing in the crosswalk who left the curb or edge of pavement at the end of the WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication to travel at a walking speed of 3.5 feet per second to at least the far side of the traveled way or to a median of sufficient width for pedestrians to wait." - "Where pedestrians who walk slower than 3.5 feet per second, or pedestrians who use wheelchairs, routinely use the crosswalk, a walking speed of less than 3.5 feet per second should be considered in determining the pedestrian clearance time." Options (permitted): - The additional time provided by an extended push button press to satisfy pedestrian clearance time needs may be added to either the walk interval or the pedestrian change interval. - The countdown display is optional for Pedestrian Change Intervals of 7 seconds or less (Figure 4I-4 footnote). - The Buffer Interval may be used to help satisfy the calculated pedestrian clearance time, or may begin after the calculated pedestrian clearance time has ended (Figure 4I-4 footnote). Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 4I-4 shows the interval sequence — steady UPRAISED HAND, then Walk Interval ("7 seconds MIN."), then Pedestrian Change Interval (flashing hand with countdown, spanning the calculated pedestrian clearance time), then Buffer Interval (steady hand, "2 seconds MIN.") — along with five possible relationships to the vehicular yellow change and red clearance intervals. - [Image 2] shows the same Figure 4I-4 in page context together with the Guidance establishing the 3.5 feet-per-second walking speed and the Option allowing up to 4 feet per second where an extended push button press function is installed. - [Image 3] shows the related Standard that the pedestrian change interval shall begin immediately after the WALKING PERSON indication and that a buffer interval of a steady UPRAISED HAND shall be displayed for at least 2 seconds prior to the release of any conflicting vehicular movement. - [Image 4] shows continuation text of Section 4I.06 concerning leading pedestrian intervals and green extensions beyond the pedestrian clearance time. - [Image 5] concerns pedestrian hybrid beacon operation and is not directly needed for this answer. Citations: - Section 4I.06 Support §6 (p.724) - Section 4I.06 Guidance §7 (p.724) - Section 4I.06 Option §9 (p.725) - Section 4I.06 Guidance §10 (p.725) - Figure 4I-4 (p.724) - Page 765 - Page 764 - Page 767
gold_answer: The order is WALK, flashing DONT WALK pedestrian change interval, then steady DONT WALK buffer interval. The buffer interval is at least 2 seconds before conflicting traffic is released, and clearance is normally evaluated using 3.5 feet per second.
